health_contribution_base_rate.basis: Re-founded as the health fund's rate (G26 A, DEC-2026-11-25-30): 3.80% from the January 2035 endpoint is the share of the fund's cost the contribution pays, about 29% of its new cost in FY2040 (health_fund.contribution_share), at the fold's price (about $56B a quarter point in FY2040, grown on HCU's path). It was booked in step 7 as the fallback that closed the whole general fund (DEC-2026-11-20-07, memo G3 E); under DEC-2026-11-25-12 it is set against health's costs. From FY2041 it moves only by the health fund's own rule (G27 A, DEC-2026-11-25-31; settlement_booking.rate_rule writes the path), which replaces memo G8's question, G16 B's second leg and G18 D's step-down.
health_contribution_base_rate.path_basis: The rate by year from FY2041 under the fund's rule: a quarter point at most once a year when the reserve, projected one year ahead, leaves 15-25% of the contribution's share of the fund's cost; never below 3.25%. Decided (G27.1a A, DEC-2026-11-26-01): the band is on the contribution's own share of the fund's cost, tested one year ahead (dossiers/foundations/fair-financing/2-settlement.md part 8).

health_fund.basis: The plan's health fund (HLT-7.22) booked as its own account (DEC-2026-11-25-12; the booking rule, DEC-2026-11-25-28; G26 A and G27 A point 2, DEC-2026-11-25-30, -31): recovery-budget/model.py's health_fund() sums these booked lines into the fund's sources and spending, the general fund pays the fund only its transfer, and the fund keeps FY2030-34's surplus, $250B of it as a standing reserve and the rest drawn to lower the FY2035 transfer. Increments to CBO's baseline. HI's own line (HI H1a and Part A HLT-6 share, the $425B) stays HI's until HI folds in at 2035, so it is not listed. The wealth tax (HS2, net of the stack cap S04) is one of the fund's sources by statute (G27 A point 1). The scope is DEC-2026-11-15-20's health rows and HX, with long-term care from 2035 (DEC-2026-11-11-02).
health_fund.standing_reserve_basis: Decided (G29 R2, DEC-2026-11-26-03; DEC-2026-11-25-31 point 2 as far as the money goes): the fund keeps a $250B standing reserve and draws the rest of FY2030-34's surplus, net of its own shortfalls in those years, against the FY2035 transfer; from the 2035 fold-in the general fund pays the whole shortfall. Memo G29 put the surplus at $307.9B, so the draw at $57.9B, with OASDI's part at the working 0.297; booked at the sourced 0.28 (source_shares) the surplus and the draw are slightly larger (notes/health-trust-fund-results.md part 3). Point 2's $141B draw would need money that is Social Security's, not health's (2-settlement.md part 8)
health_fund.source_shares_basis: Social Security's part of the tax on former premiums is left out of the fund's sources (G29, DEC-2026-11-26-03). HX (the tax on former premiums) and HEX (the part of it the employer contribution takes back) both carry the payroll tax current law credits to OASDI (ledger-revenue.csv's HX note; dossiers/care/6-cost.md item 4), which can't be health money (DEC-2026-11-25-12, -28), so both take the same weight (G29, finding 3; #507 weighted HX only). The weight is 0.72: OASDI's part is 0.28 of the net exclusion revenue, range 0.22-0.30, as memo G29 sources it (payroll 36-38% of the exclusion, OASDI about 78% of payroll; EV-FIN-094, EV-FIN-095). Step 11's working 0.297 is replaced now that G29 is decided, as this basis said it would be. Where the OASDI part goes is social_security_part

social_security_part.basis: Decided (G29 A, DEC-2026-11-26-03): the OASDI part of HX and HEX (1 - source_shares) is credited to Social Security's trust funds from FY2031, the first year HX exists, as current law does (42 U.S.C. 401(a)); no law in the plan diverts Social Security payroll tax from the trust funds. recovery-budget/model.py's social_security_part() takes it off the general fund; funds-model.py books it as HX-SS (funds-ss-hx.csv's hx_ss_pct_payroll, written by settlement_booking.py --write). Unified figures don't move. With the plan's package Social Security's funds last to about 2072 instead of 2061; the general fund is short in FY2035 and FY2040-44 (memo G29 part 3 and its question G29.1).

health_fund.rule_basis: G27 A (DEC-2026-11-25-31): from FY2040 the contribution (HCU with S06 and S03) pays contribution_share of the fund's spending, written by settlement_booking.py --write as its FY2040 yield at 3.80% over that year's spending (G26 A); the general fund's transfer in law is the rest of the cost after the fund's other sources; the fund's reserve absorbs the difference between the contribution's yield and its share. band, step and floor are the decided rule's (point 1); the band's base is the contribution's own share of the fund's cost, tested one year ahead (G27.1a A, DEC-2026-11-26-01).
